what_its_for: Alclometasone dipropionate is a mild steroid cream or ointment used to relieve redness, itching, swelling, and discomfort caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, allergic rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only. Wash your hands before and after applying. Gently clean and dry the affected area. Apply a thin layer of the cream or ointment to the affected skin and rub it in gently. Do not cover the treated area with bandages, plastic wrap, or tight clothing unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2 to 3 times daily, or exactly as directed by your doctor. Do not use more than prescribed, and do not use it more often or for longer than recommended. Using too much or for too long can increase the risk of side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed one and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tube or container tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Do not store in the bathroom where heat and moisture can damage the medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using this medicine on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as the skin in these areas absorbs more medicine and may be more prone to side effects. Do not use on open wounds, cuts, or infected skin. Avoid using cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products on treated areas without asking your doctor first. Avoid prolonged sun exposure on treated skin. Do not share this medication with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if your skin condition does not improve within 2 weeks of treatment, or if it gets worse. Also call your doctor if you notice any signs of skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, or pus; if you develop thinning, discoloration, or stretch marks on the skin; if you experience unusual weight gain, tiredness, swelling of the face or ankles, or increased thirst or urination, which could be signs that the medication is being absorbed into your body. Seek immediate medical attention if you have signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Many people notice improvement in redness, itching, and swelling within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks. If you do not see improvement after 2 weeks, talk to your doctor before continuing use.
special_populations: Children: Use with caution in children, as they are more likely to absorb the medicine through the skin and experience side effects. Avoid using on large areas of skin, under diapers, or with tight coverings on children. Use the smallest amount needed for the shortest time possible. Elderly: Older adults may have thinner, more fragile skin, so use carefully and follow your doctor's guidance. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Use only if your doctor decides the benefits outweigh the risks. If breastfeeding, do not apply to the chest or breast area to avoid accidental exposure to your baby.
